strengths: Well-motivated problem: clearly articulates limitations of grid-based Gaussian allocation and provides principled alternative with sub-pixel placement
Significant practical efficiency: achieves 7x reduction in primitives compared to pixel-aligned baselines while improving reconstruction quality
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: tested on two datasets (DL3DV, Charge) with multiple baselines, detailed ablations validating each component
Solid technical execution: proper use of DSNT for differentiable coordinate extraction, entropy-based adaptive density allocation, multi-view confidence learning integrated coherently
Strong empirical results: achieves state-of-the-art on pose-free feed-forward 3DGS across metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS) on DL3DV benchmark
Valuable secondary insight: demonstrates that rendering-supervised fine-tuning can improve backbone camera pose estimation, unlike AnySplat, suggesting promise for self-supervised 3D model refinement
Quality of analysis: interpretable visualizations (Figures 4-5) showing learned spatial distributions and multi-view reasoning behavior
Good ablation studies: Table 3 systematically validates contribution of detection, adaptive density, and confidence components
weaknesses: Limited fundamental novelty: individual components are from prior work (DSNT from Nibali et al., entropy-based allocation from APT); contribution is primarily combinatorial rather than introducing new concepts

Strong dependency on VGGT backbone: method cannot fix geometric errors from the foundation model; inherits failures (masked sky pixels, specularities, reflective surfaces) that hurt downstream reconstruction

Weakened self-supervised claim: teacher geometry losses (L_depth, L_R, L_t) that regularize to VGGT make this distillation-based rather than purely self-supervised, potentially limiting improvements beyond the teacher model

Hyperparameter choices lack justification: entropy allocation thresholds (55/35/15%), primitive counts per density level (16/32/64), and regularization weights (e.g., L_op = Σ sin(α·c)) appear arbitrary without sensitivity analysis or ablation
Incomplete sparse view evaluation: experiments use 3-12 views; 1-2 view performance on pose-free scenarios unexplored despite high practical relevance
Modest improvements over closest baseline: only ~1-2 PSNR point gains over AnySplat on DL3DV, raising questions about practical significance despite efficiency improvements
Background reconstruction issues: acknowledged failure on Charge sparse splits due to lack of covisibility; suggests limitations when camera trajectories don't constrain backgrounds
Depth degradation on synthetic data: Table 2 shows slight depth metric decrease on Charge despite claimed improvements, explained away as background overfitting but raising generalization concerns
Experimental design concerns: FLARE test-time alignment completely fails making comparison uninformative; DepthSplat baseline uses same VGGT backbone making decoder contribution unclear
No statistical significance testing: results lack error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests across multiple runs
Incomplete scene reconstruction acknowledged: method only reconstructs visible geometry, leaving holes—fundamental feed-forward limitation affecting practical applicability
Test-time complexity underexplored: pose-free evaluation requires second forward pass (N+T views) doubling inference cost, not prominently discussed
Missing implementation details: code availability not mentioned, no runtime/memory comparisons with baselines, training convergence not discussed
Loss function complexity under-analyzed: photometric + geometry consistency + teacher geometry + regularization losses interact in unclear ways; critical loss components not fully ablated

strengths: Novel off-grid primitive detection mechanism using differentiable heatmaps addresses a real limitation of regular grid-based methods
Strong visual results demonstrating cleaner geometry and better detail preservation compared to baselines, especially in extrapolated views
Adaptive density mechanism using Shannon entropy for principled primitive allocation, validated through comprehensive ablations showing 7x fewer primitives
Well-integrated technical pipeline with multiple complementary loss functions (photometric, geometry consistency, regularization) and thorough implementation details
Good ablation studies (Tables 3-4) validating each component's contribution to final performance
weaknesses: Quantitative improvements over baselines are marginal (PSNR differences ~0.5-1.0 dB in Table 1) without statistical significance testing or confidence intervals
Architectural novelty is incremental—most components (VGGT backbone, U-Net decoder, standard losses) are conventional; core novelty limited to Gaussian primitive detection
Novel view synthesis evaluation relies heavily on qualitative visual assessment despite being a key contribution, with limited quantitative metrics
Evaluation conducted at reduced resolution (maximum 518 pixels) rather than full resolution; missing critical inference time and speed comparisons
Technical clarity gaps: soft-max positioning (Eq. 1) appears overly simplistic without justification; relationship between 2D heatmap detection and 3D primitive placement needs clarification
Unresolved technical limitations (half-transparent objects, view-dependent colors, scene holes) acknowledged but not addressed, limiting practical applicability
Reproducibility concerns: no code availability mentioned, training time/computational requirements unspecified, no variance analysis across multiple runs
Limited failure case analysis—Section 5 acknowledges limitations but lacks systematic investigation of when and why the method fails compared to baselines
Potential fairness issues in baseline comparisons (different training data, using VGGT supervision may provide unfair advantage, missing recent concurrent methods)
Design choices appear pragmatic rather than principled (bilinear interpolation for Gaussian parameters, entropy threshold of 86% for adaptive density not justified)

strengths: Novel off-the-grid primitive detection mechanism that achieves sub-pixel precision with adaptive density allocation based on Shannon entropy, addressing real limitations of grid-based approaches

Strong empirical results: achieves superior visual quality on novel view synthesis while using 7× fewer primitives than AnySplat, with significant improvements in geometric accuracy (depth RMSE, camera pose estimation)

Comprehensive experimental validation across 6 diverse datasets with thorough ablation studies (Table 3) demonstrating the contribution of each component; clear superiority in qualitative comparisons (Figure 7)

Well-engineered architecture combining VGGT backbone, heatmap-based detection, and multi-view aggregation with confidence-weighted selection; technically sound approach with appropriate loss functions
Practical efficiency and applicability: generates high-quality 3DGS models in seconds without 3D annotations, enabling real-world deployment on resource-constrained systems
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (Figures 1-9) that clearly communicate the method; detailed implementation specifications support reproducibility
weaknesses: Individual technical components are adaptations of existing techniques (VGGT backbone, entropy-based allocation, multi-view fusion); main novelty lies in their combination rather than introducing fundamentally new methods, limiting core originality

Limited baseline comparisons: primary evaluation focuses on AnySplat with only brief mentions of other recent pose-free methods; missing thorough comparisons with concurrent approaches like FreeSplat and 4DGT mentioned in related work

Insufficient technical clarity in critical sections: Section 3.2 (Gaussian Decoder) is dense and lacks intuitive explanation; multi-view aggregation strategy (how confidences are used to weight/select primitives) needs clearer exposition
Hyperparameter sensitivity not thoroughly analyzed: entropy thresholds (55% medium, 15% high density) appear arbitrary without ablation; no sensitivity analysis for key hyperparameters

Incomplete failure case analysis: Section 5 mentions missing cube face problem but provides limited systematic discussion of failure modes; when does adaptive density allocation fail? When does off-the-grid detection produce worse results?
Confidence mechanism under-specified: mechanism for pruning low-confidence primitives at test time is unclear; whether pruning is applied during rendering or disabled at inference needs clarification

Missing computational analysis: wall-clock training time comparison with baselines not provided despite 7× fewer primitives claim; memory usage during training/inference and complexity analysis of detection modules absent

Evaluation scope limitation: most datasets are indoor/controlled scenarios; limited evaluation on large-scale complex outdoor scenes or extreme view variations; no user study for perceptual quality assessment
